thread:
Zoey: Heads-up: weird repro where Vite/Rollup pick .js entry and webpack picks .mjs -> runtime mismatch on Edge. Error: "TypeError: createEmbedding is not a function" only after minified prod build.
Arun: wait, different extensions? how is package.json exports defined?
Zoey: SDK exports: {
  ".": {
    "import": "dist/index.mjs",
    "require": "dist/index.cjs"
  },
  "./feature": {
    "import": "dist/feature.mjs",
    "require": "dist/feature.cjs"
  }
} and package also ships dist/index.js (CJS transpiled to .js) for legacy tools.
Camila: Many bundlers prefer file extension heuristics when fields not present or when plugin resolves by extension order. Which bundler picked which?
Zoey: Repro matrix: Vite (rollup resolver) resolved to dist/index.js (legacy) -> produced bundle that worked in Node but failed on Vercel Edge with `createEmbedding is not a function`. webpack with experiments.outputModule:true resolved dist/index.mjs and worked. Rollup sometimes flipped based on plugin order.
Arun: createEmbedding is a named export on the ESM build but in the legacy .js it was exported as `module.exports = { default: ..., createEmbedding: undefined }` due to a build bug in our CJS rollup step. So when bundle picked .js, the function was missing. When it picked .mjs, it was fine.
Zoey: Exactly. The confusing part: local dev (unbundled) uses ESM entry and works; prod bundle picks the wrong file because some consumers and plugins resolve `.js` before `.mjs` when `mainFields` include `main` or `browser`.
Camila: Quick repro steps?
Zoey: minimal:
1) git clone https://example.com/repro-ext-resolve.git
2) npm ci
3) npm run build:vite (prod) -> inspect dist/vendor.js; run node --input-type=module dist/server.js or deploy to Edge
4) npm run build:webpack (prod) -> same check
Observed: Vite build logs: `[plugin:node-resolve] resolved redwood-inference -> node_modules/redwood-inference/dist/index.js (prefers .js)`
Arun: Workarounds on consumer side: force resolver mainFields to prefer `module`/`import` or add `resolve.conditions` so rollup picks the import condition. For webpack: set `resolve.extensions: ['.mjs','.js','.json']` and `mainFields:['module','main']`.
Camila: SDK-side fixes: 1) remove legacy dist/index.js to avoid extension confusion; 2) add explicit `exports['./'] = { import: './dist/index.mjs', default: './dist/index.cjs', browser: './dist/index.browser.mjs' }` including a browser condition; 3) ensure CJS build correctly exports named functions (fix the CJS bundler shim).
Zoey: I opened an issue with the repro and logs. ops-bot: CI build report: bundle-check failed on branch fix/exports-ext: `createEmbedding is not a function` - https://ci.example.com/issue/7234
Arun: Also add a CI smoke test that builds a tiny app with different resolvers and asserts the bundle exports contain `createEmbedding` (simple typeof check in node --input-type=module). That would have caught the bad CJS shim.
Camila: Agree. I'll propose an SDK PR: remove ambiguous .js artifacts, add exports.browser, and fix CJS interop plus add the smoke tests. Meanwhile I'll add a short note in README troubleshooting about extension resolution and bundler config snippets.
Zoey: Thanks. I'll attach the failing vendor snippet and the minimal repro link in the issue and assign to @pkg-maintainers. ops-bot: CI job bundle-matrix failed: see https://ci.example.com/runs/7234 for logs.
Arun: One more gotcha: Vite's dependency pre-bundling (esbuild) sometimes rewrites imports and can inline the wrong file; add `optimizeDeps.exclude: ['redwood-inference']` in Vite consumer for a short-term workaround.
Zoey: Good call. I'll include that in the docs. Will post PR link here when ready. :shipit:
